title: Colorful skies over Paranal Observatory
caption: The Milky Way over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This view from ESO's Paranal Observatory shows the Milky Way above the Very Large Telescope (VLT), with three of its four Unit Telescopes in the frame. The photograph, credited to P. Horálek/ESO, carries the title Colorful skies over Paranal Observatory.

The VLT's Unit Telescopes can work together as a giant interferometer. Combining their light in this way lets astronomers see much finer detail than any one telescope could. ESO describes the VLT as the world's most advanced optical instrument.

The Milky Way looks richly detailed here, but a single VLT telescope can pick out objects some four billion times fainter than the unaided eye can see. That power has opened a new age of discoveries, and the VLT has notched up several notable scientific firsts, among them the first image of a planet outside our Solar System.
